paragraphs: At the very heart of Ravenwood stood an ancient beech tree whose branches almost reached the clouds. Two unusual neighbours lived among its spreading boughs. One was Ozzy, a young but clever and sensible owl, a true gentleman who loved his soft armchair and good books above all else. The other was Fifi, a mischievous, irresponsible ten-year-old fairy who was always ready for fun and never for worries.
That day, Fifi was sitting among the thick leaves at the very top of the tree. Smiling, she waved her magic wand, trying to make the little clouds change shape. Nothing happened.
“That’s the trouble with magic,” she thought with a sigh. “Lots of fun, but nothing to show for it.”
Suddenly, her tummy began to rumble.
“Oh, time to go home. I need something to eat,” she decided.

She fluttered down from the high branch, her tiny wings whirling through the air. In a few moments, she reached her cottage, cleverly hidden among the mighty boughs. She opened the fridge at once. The sight of its empty shelves left her speechless.
“What’s happened here? Where’s all my food?” she asked herself. “There’s always been something to eat in my fridge. I’d better pop over to Ozzy’s and ask him about this strange business!”

Without waiting for her tummy to rumble again, she left her cottage and flew up to the little door in Ozzy’s hollow on a higher branch. She flew straight in without knocking. As usual, Ozzy was sitting in his red armchair, a book in his claws and spectacles perched on his beak. This time, though, he looked distinctly displeased to see her.
“Fifi, where are your manners? Couldn’t you knock? Why must you burst in making such a racket?” he asked.
“Sorry, Ozzy, but I’m terribly worried!” she replied. “There’s nothing to eat at home. And I’m hungry!”
“Calm down, Fifi. How did you come to be hungry? Where do you usually get your food?”
“Where do you think? From the fridge! But it must be broken, because there’s nothing inside!” she sighed, putting her hands on her hips.
“An empty fridge isn’t broken. Someone’s forgotten to fill it,” said Ozzy, unable to hide a little smile. “Where do you get your supplies?”
“I don’t. They’ve always been in the fridge. What about you, Ozzy? Where do you get yours?”
“I hunt or gather food in the forest. If you like, I can take you to pick blueberries. That’s a splendid way to stock up your fridge.”

They set off at once. Ozzy led the way, spreading his powerful wings. He glided calmly and confidently, like a proper guide. Fifi tried to keep up, but her delicate, transparent wings were not nearly as strong. Every so often, the owl stopped on a branch to wait for the breathless fairy.

It was a long journey. They passed old trees with roots like enormous snakes and clearings filled with fragrant heather. Sunlight filtered through the canopy, and the air smelled of damp woodland. After more than an hour, they arrived.
They landed gently beside some blueberry bushes. Purple berries gleamed in the sunshine. Fifi eagerly tucked into the first ones she found.
“These are delicious!” said Fifi. “Much better than the food in my fridge. They taste like pure sunshine!”
“And they’re nourishing,” he added. “These sweet berries are full of sugar, vitamins and minerals. A real treasure of the forest!”
“It’s a shame these treasures grow so far away,” Fifi mumbled through a mouthful. “What if we moved these bushes closer to home? Then we’d always have food nearby!”
Ozzy raised an eyebrow and looked at her thoughtfully.
“Moving bushes like these is risky. They might not take root in a new place. But we could grow some brand-new ones of our own.”
“Let’s do that!” Fifi clapped her hands with excitement. “I want my own blueberries right beside my cottage!”

After their meal, Fifi tucked two blueberries under her arm to save for later. Smiling, with their tummies full, they set off for home. The forest whispered softly around them, as though it were listening to their new plan.

When they reached home, they got straight to work. Fifi eagerly searched the ground around the beech tree for the best place to make a garden. At last, she chose a sunny patch near the stream. Ozzy watched approvingly, then began to explain:

“We need to turn the soil over to bring the rich, dark earth to the surface. That’s called digging. We must pull out all the weeds and roots, too, or they’ll get in our plants’ way. Here’s a little spade. You make a start, and I’ll fetch the seeds.”

Fifi set to work eagerly. She turned over every patch of soil, pulling out weeds and roots as she went. When she had finished, she did something extra: she made a low fence around the bed, weaving willow twigs between little sticks she had pushed upright into the ground.
When Ozzy returned with a bag of seeds, he smiled broadly and hooted with approval:
“Hoo, hoo! Wonderful work, Fifi! I haven’t seen such lovely soil in a long time!”
Fifi stood up proudly and brushed the dirt from her hands.
“Do you really like it?” she asked with a smile.

“Very much. Now for the next step,” said Ozzy, handing her the seeds. “Dig a small hole for each seed and put it in the soil. Let’s make three rows. We’ll plant blueberries in the first two and tomatoes in the last. Those are the bigger seeds. We only have three of them.”
“Why only three tomatoes?” Fifi asked in surprise.
“That will be plenty for us,” Ozzy replied with a smile. “Tomatoes are very big vegetables.”
Fifi carefully planted the seeds as she had been told. Meanwhile, Ozzy went to the stream for water. When he returned with a full bucket, he watered the little planting holes and explained:
“This is the last step. Whenever you plant something, you must water the soil. From now on, we’ll need to look after our garden every day.”
Fifi gazed at the neatly sown rows and sighed contentedly. In her mind, she could already see blueberry bushes growing and becoming covered in sweet berries.

Early the next morning, just as the sun was peeping over the horizon, Fifi fluttered down to the garden. She looked around and was disappointed to find that it looked exactly as it had the day before. Not a single little plant had appeared above the soil.
“How much longer do I have to wait? This is ridiculous!” she grumbled impatiently. “I’ll starve before the first berries appear. I’m going to cast a spell. Magic is bound to help!”
She took out her wand and was just about to say the spell when a familiar hoot sounded behind her:

“Stop, Fifi!” Ozzy flew down from a branch and caught her hand just above the garden bed. “How many times have I told you that magic isn’t for getting whatever you fancy? It’s a great responsibility! You can’t go casting spells on nature without a thought.”
“But why not?” asked the fairy crossly. “It’s only a little bit of magic.”
“Nature doesn’t like being interfered with,” Ozzy explained. “If you start casting spells left and right, the plants might rebel.”
Fifi gave a heavy sigh.
“What am I supposed to do, then? No berries, no garden. Just hunger and boredom!”

“Hungry, bored and grumbling!” Ozzy laughed. “Don’t be so impatient! If you like, we could try a little learning experiment. Let’s enchant one seedling. Just one! Then we can see how a plant grows and how nature responds to all this hocus-pocus.”
Fifi brightened, then crouched beside one of the rows. She chose the smallest seedling and took hold of her wand.
“All right! One little experiment!”
She closed her eyes and murmured a spell:
“Accelerans incrementum!”
Suddenly, the soil beneath the little plant trembled. White roots, thin as threads, began to grow from the seed and spread in every direction.
“Look, Ozzy!” cried Fifi.
A moment later, a stem appeared above the soil. At first, it was thin and delicate, but soon it split in two, and two tiny, pale green leaves unfolded at its tips.
“Amazing!” the fairy whispered, clutching her wand.
“Nature is always amazing,” Ozzy added with a smile. “Even without magic.”
The stem grew very quickly, split in two, and then new branches began to sprout from each little twig. Fresh green leaves appeared just as quickly and grew before their very eyes.
When the plant was big, green buds appeared at its tips. Soon they opened their petals to reveal tiny white flowers, like little porcelain bells. Fifi clapped her hands.
“It’s wonderful!” said the fairy, her wings fluttering with joy.
Small, buzzing insects flew straight to the flowers, landing on one and then another.
“Those are bees,” Ozzy explained. “They help the flowers make fruit by carrying pollen from one flower to another.”
A warm breeze blew the petals away, revealing tiny green balls beneath them: the promise of berries to come.
“What’s happening now?” Fifi asked in surprise. “Where have my beautiful flowers gone?”
“Flowers are only a short stage in a plant’s life,” Ozzy explained. “After pollination, they turn into fruit. Keep watching carefully, Fifi.”

The little green balls began to change colour. First, they turned pink, then darker, until at last they were a deep purple. Fifi recognised them at once: blueberries! She reached out to pick one, but Ozzy stopped her.
“Don’t touch those berries, Fifi. They grew with the help of a spell. They might harm you. Besides, nature’s show isn’t over yet.”

Fifi drew back her hand and watched curiously. The berries turned a deep purple. Then they began to shrivel and fall from the bush, one by one. When they reached the ground, they grew soft and started to decay.
“Oh no! All that work for nothing!” Fifi folded her arms, her face clouding over. “I only wanted one little berry…”

“Look closely,” Ozzy said softly. “The fruit is dying, but it’s uncovering the seeds inside. If they fall on good soil, they can grow into new bushes. But not this time. These enchanted berries will not bring new life.”
Slowly, the bush began to wither. Its little leaves dried out, turned gold and red, and then started falling to the ground.
“Your little bush, my fairy friend, has just got itself ready for winter,” Ozzy explained.
“What? But it’s the middle of summer!” cried Fifi.

“It’s because of your spell that speeds up time,” Ozzy said sadly. “It’s lived its whole life in just a few moments. It won’t make it to winter. I think it will wither away, and there’ll be nothing left of it.”

Fifi lowered her head. Something more than sadness stirred in her heart: understanding. You couldn’t push nature along with spells to make it do whatever you wanted. The rhythm of the natural world had to be left undisturbed.
“Oh, Ozzy, you’re so wise. I’m glad you’re my friend. I’ll wait patiently for the rest of the berries. And until then, I’ll look for fruit in the forest.”

And so Fifi learned that nature keeps its own time and cannot be hurried. She understood that the true fruits of our work come from patience, care and respect for the natural world. She also learned about the cycle of a plant’s growth: from a seed to flowers and fruit, then fading away and new life growing from the seeds hidden inside.
And if you’d like to find out what happened next to the young fairy and Ozzy, come and read the story of the drought that came to Ravenwood.
